parsed.explanation: The quoted dichotomy is verbatim and is used essentially: Lemma 1 invokes "b = g(z) \in \{0,c\} (because V \subseteq \{0,c\})", and §7 concludes from S_0 = ∅ that g ≡ c. But §3 only proves that V contains at most one POSITIVE number; nothing there or anywhere else in the text excludes negative values of g. The only remark on sign is "g(x) > -x", which does not give g ≥ 0. So the step from "at most one positive value" to "V ⊆ {0,c}" does not follow. The objector's repair is also correct: if g(x) = d < 0, then (4) gives g(x+nd) = d by induction, and each x+nd = f(x+(n-1)d) > 0, contradicting x+nd → -∞. Since this fact is needed but never proved, the necessity/structural obligation is incomplete as written.
